I have been farming these 10.1 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. I finished primary school, and after that I learned everything from the field and from watching others. My husband and me, we are two people in the house, and he sometimes goes to the city for construction work to bring extra cash. That means most days I am the one watching the crops.

Last year I kept 7 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and planted 3.1 mu of cotton. The wheat gave about 500 jin per mu, the maize was close to 600 jin, and cotton was around 250 jin of seed cotton. Prices were not great, but we did not lose money. This year I will do almost the same, because changing a working plan is risky. I saw old Wang cut his fertilizer last year to save money, and his wheat came up thin and yellow. I am not making that mistake. Fertilizer is expensive—urea went up again at the cooperative—but a bad harvest is a disaster, while wasting some fertilizer is only a cost.

For the winter wheat on the 7 mu, I will buy improved seed from the dealer, the same kind my neighbor Zhang used with good results. I will rotary-till the ground before sowing in October. For fertilizer, I put one 50kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base—that is the 15-15-15 type—so that gives 7.5 jin of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium each. Then at green-up I spread one full 50kg bag of urea per mu, which is about 23 jin of nitrogen. If the plants look yellow at heading, I add another half bag. I irrigate three times: once in winter if there is no snow, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. The well pump costs electricity, but we need it. I spray twice: herbicide right after sowing, and one insecticide at heading when the aphids come.

For the summer maize on the same 7 mu, I plant hybrid seed immediately after cutting the wheat in June. There is no time to plough—you miss the moisture and the heat, and the yield drops. I use the no-till seeder. I put one 40kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu in the row at sowing, then topdress with one 40kg bag of urea at the big trumpet stage. That is about 18 jin of nitrogen from the urea plus 6 jin from the compound. I irrigate twice: once in June if it is dry, and once in July when the ears are forming. Two sprays: herbicide and one for corn borer.

For cotton on the 3.1 mu, I plough in spring because cotton likes loose soil. I plant hybrid cotton seed, the kind with the big bolls that the dealer says resists disease. I put one 50kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and topdress with 30kg of urea twice—once at flowering and once at boll setting. I irrigate three times: flowering, boll setting, and boll opening. Cotton needs more medicine than grain. I spray four times: herbicide once, and insecticide three times for bollworm and aphids. If you skip a spray, the worms eat the bolls and you cry.

I worry about every yuan, but I would rather sleep soundly knowing I fed my crops well.
